questions.stem: What type of reaction occurs when bromine adds across the C=C double bond of an alkene?
questions.explanation: When bromine reacts with an alkene, it is an addition reaction. The double bond opens up and each bromine atom adds to one of the carbon atoms, forming a dibromo compound.

questions.stem: What is produced when ethene reacts with steam in the presence of a catalyst?
questions.explanation: Ethene reacts with steam (hydration) in the presence of a phosphoric acid catalyst to produce ethanol: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH. This is an addition reaction.

questions.stem: What is produced when ethene reacts with hydrogen gas using a nickel catalyst?
questions.explanation: Ethene + hydrogen → ethane (C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆). This is hydrogenation, an addition reaction where hydrogen adds across the double bond, producing a saturated alkane.

questions.stem: Why can alkenes undergo addition reactions but alkanes cannot?

options.text: Alkenes have a C=C double bond that can open up to form new bonds

questions.explanation: The C=C double bond in alkenes can break open (one of the two bonds breaks) to allow other atoms to add across, forming two new single bonds. Alkanes have no double bond to open up.

questions.stem: What is the name of the product formed when ethene reacts with hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
questions.explanation: Ethene + HCl → chloroethane (CH₃CH₂Cl). The H and Cl atoms add across the double bond in an addition reaction.

questions.stem: How many products are formed in a typical addition reaction of an alkene?
questions.explanation: Addition reactions produce only one product. The two reactant molecules join together completely, with no atoms left over. This is different from substitution reactions, which produce two products.

questions.stem: What is the industrial importance of the reaction between ethene and steam?

options.text: It removes pollutants from the air
It is used to manufacture ethanol for use as a solvent and fuel

questions.explanation: The hydration of ethene with steam is the main industrial method for producing ethanol, which is used as a solvent, fuel additive, and in the manufacture of other chemicals.
